headline_marked: Netrokona: [[Youth allegedly sets shopkeeper on fire]] over cigarette credit
headline: Netrokona: Youth allegedly sets shopkeeper on fire over cigarette credit
summary: A grocery store owner is in critical condition after a youth allegedly sprayed fuel and ignited the shop when refused cigarettes on credit.
details: A grocery shop owner suffered severe burns after a youth allegedly set his shop on fire in Netrokona's Kendua upazila on Thursday night.
The incident occurred around 10:30pm at Sahitpur Bazar in Sandikona union, leaving the victim, Ibrahim Khalil, 45, in critical condition.
According to police and locals, the accused, Suman Miah, frequently took goods from the shop on credit without paying.
Kendua Police Station OC Md Tarikul Islam stated that Suman demanded cigarettes on credit on Thursday, leading to an argument when the owner refused.
The accused allegedly used fuel oil from a bottle displayed for sale in front of the shop to spray the interior and set it ablaze.
The fire quickly engulfed the shop, causing severe injuries to Khalil and destroying most of the store's inventory.
Khalil was initially rushed to Kendua Upazila Health Complex, then referred to Mymensingh Medical College Hospital, and finally admitted to the burn unit of Dhaka Medical College Hospital.
Police are currently conducting drives to arrest Suman Miah, while the victim's family intends to file a formal case upon their return from Dhaka.
caption:
Refused cigarettes on credit, and he set the shop on fire. A shopkeeper is now fighting for his life in a burn unit.

A grocery shop owner suffered severe burns after a youth allegedly set his shop on fire in Netrokona's Kendua upazila on Thursday night.

The incident occurred around 10:30pm at Sahitpur Bazar in Sandikona union, leaving the victim, Ibrahim Khalil, 45, in critical condition.

According to police and locals, the accused, Suman Miah, frequently took goods from the shop on credit without paying.

Kendua Police Station OC Md Tarikul Islam stated that Suman demanded cigarettes on credit on Thursday, leading to an argument when the owner refused.

The accused allegedly used fuel oil from a bottle displayed for sale in front of the shop to spray the interior and set it ablaze.

The fire quickly engulfed the shop, causing severe injuries to Khalil and destroying most of the store's inventory.

Khalil was initially rushed to Kendua Upazila Health Complex, then referred to Mymensingh Medical College Hospital, and finally admitted to the burn unit of Dhaka Medical College Hospital.

Police are currently conducting drives to arrest Suman Miah, while the victim's family intends to file a formal case upon their return from Dhaka.

headline_marked: Measles outbreak: [[Four more die]] in 24 hours, total toll reaches 1,114
headline: Measles outbreak: Four more die in 24 hours, total toll reaches 1,114
summary: Bangladesh records four more deaths from measles in the last 24 hours, bringing the total fatalities to 1,114. The Directorate General of Health Services reports 21 new confirmed cases.
details: Four more people have died with measles symptoms in Bangladesh, and 21 new cases have been confirmed nationwide. The latest deaths bring the total toll involving suspected measles symptoms this year to 1,012. Confirmed measles deaths stand at 102, pushing the combined total to 1,114.

Dhaka Division has reported the highest number of deaths related to suspected measles, with 455 fatalities. Sylhet follows with 179 deaths, while Rajshahi has reported 93, Chattogram 86, Mymensingh 80, Barishal 60, Khulna 44, and Rangpur 15.

Over the 24-hour period ending Thursday morning, 1,221 patients sought hospital care, with 1,144 admitted. Dhaka Division saw the highest number of new admissions with 377, followed by Chattogram (261) and Sylhet (143).

Since March 15, the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has recorded a total of 172,021 hospital admissions linked to measles and suspected cases. Of these, 166,933 patients have recovered and been discharged.

The total number of reported suspected measles cases has reached 194,084, with 21,623 confirmed. The DGHS notes that not all patients are tested, so the actual confirmed case count may be higher than recorded figures, which primarily cover those who received hospital care.
